title: Feasts ranked as God’s own cult—yet Saint-days abound; many say they are God’s feasts in Saints’ memory
source_text: XXVI. Ad festa quod attinet, Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores solent quidem illa numerare inter ea quae ad cultum Deo proprium pertinent: et tamen in Ecclesia Romana solemne est dies festos instituere in honorem Sanctorum. Ut autem ista concilient, Dicunt eorum multi festa quae dicuntur Sanctorum, non Sanctis proprie, sed Deo dicari, verum in memoriam & honorem Sanctorum. Quemadmodum templa soli Deo sacrantur, sed in Sanctorum quoque honorem atque Memoriam. Et similiter Missae sacrificium non offertur ulli quam Deo, & tamen hoc non obstat quominus in honorem Sanctorum Missa celebretur, ut antea fuit expositum.
pass_a_gloss: As regards feasts, the Doctors of the Roman Church are indeed accustomed to number them among the things that pertain to the cult proper to God: and yet in the Roman Church it is solemn to institute feast days in honor of the Saints. But that they may reconcile these things, many of them say that the feasts which are called of the Saints are dedicated not properly to the Saints, but to God, yet in memory and honor of the Saints. Just as temples are consecrated to God alone, but also in the honor and Memory of the Saints. And likewise the sacrifice of the Mass is offered to none but God, and yet this does not hinder that Mass be celebrated in honor of the Saints, as was explained before.
pass_b_english: Feasts are classed with Godward cult—yet Saint-days fill the calendar.
Many resolve it: feasts (like temples and Masses) go to God, in the Saints’ memory and honor.

lemmas.gloss: in memory and honor of the Saints

choices.why: Feasts’ native classification before the Saint-day tension.
